definition: A full-body harness that stops a fall. Not a waist belt.
The fixed point a fall-arrest lanyard is attached to.
The line between the harness and the anchor point.
A fixed rail at an edge that stops a person from falling.
The low board at the edge of a platform that stops objects sliding off.
A temporary structure to work from at height.
A scaffold on wheels that is moved by hand.
A portable ladder.
The height above the ground or floor at which the work is done.
The outer edge of a roof, where a person can fall off.
A hole in a floor or deck that a person or an object can fall through.
Tools or materials that fall from the work area and can hit people below.
To close an area with barriers or tape so that nobody walks in.
The area where a person can be hit if something falls, swings or tips over.
A hard hat that protects the head.
The strap that keeps the helmet on the head.
Shoes or boots with a protective toe cap.
Work gloves that protect the hands.
Clothing in a signal colour with reflective bands.
Glasses that protect the eyes from dust and splinters.
How strong the wind is, measured in m/s.
To stop the job at once and not continue until the foreman says so.
A machine that lifts and moves a load hanging from a hook. In formal Polish, "dźwig" means a passenger or goods lift, not a crane.
A crane on a wheeled chassis that drives to the site.
A crane mounted on a lorry, used to load and unload it.
A truck with a telescopic boom for lifting pallets and loads.
The person who operates the crane.
The person who attaches the load to the hook and releases it.
The person who gives signals to the crane operator.
A certified strap, chain or wire that connects the load to the hook. Not a lashing strap for securing cargo.
A U-shaped metal link with a pin, used to connect lifting slings.
The crane hook the load hangs from.
A load that hangs from the crane and is off the ground.
The heaviest load a piece of lifting gear is marked to carry.
A rope tied to the load so it can be guided from a distance.
The extendable legs that keep a crane from tipping over.
Plates placed under the outriggers to spread the load on the ground.
An electric line in the air that a crane or load can touch.
The smallest distance that must be kept from a hazard.
The danger of being squeezed between the load and something fixed.
Two-way radio between the crane operator and the signaller.
Slings, shackles and other gear between the hook and the load.
Immediate help to an injured person, and the equipment for it.
The agreed place where everyone gathers in an emergency.
The person who leads the crew on site and signs the SJA.
The agreed way to get a person down who hangs in a harness after a fall.
Equipment that protects the lungs: a half mask with the right filter, or a fresh-air mask. Not an ordinary dust mask unless the data sheet allows it.
Fresh air through the room: mechanical extraction or open windows and doors, so that solvent vapour does not build up.
A liquid that dissolves paint or varnish and evaporates, e.g. white spirit. The vapour harms the nervous system and can catch fire.
Chemicals in the hardener of two-component polyurethane products. Can cause asthma. Only trained workers may use them.
The supplier's sheet for a chemical product: hazards, protective equipment, first aid, storage. Section 8 is protective equipment, section 4 first aid.
The firm's register of the hazardous chemicals in use, with their safety data sheets. Required by the regulations, kept in Norwegian, and must be easy to reach.
Fire, a lighter, a cigarette or a gas burner. Not the same as a spark from a tool.
Fresh, unset concrete or mortar. Strongly alkaline: burns the skin and the eyes.
The temporary moulds, with ties and props, that hold the concrete until it has set.
The handheld rod that is pushed into the concrete to remove air. Vibrates the hands and arms.
Ear defenders or ear plugs.
The pump and its hose that carry concrete to the pour. A blocked hose can whip when the pressure is released.
Rinsing the eye with an eye-wash bottle or clean running water.
Waste that must be kept apart and delivered to an approved receiver: paint and solvent residues, soaked rags, empty cans with residue.
